content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display device. The report also further disclosed the design details of this highly anticipated smart home hub device.

Bloomberg reported that this home hub features a 6-inch square display, with an overall design reminiscent of the classic iMac G4 — which back in the day had a hemispherical base paired with a metal stand supporting the display.

According to Mark Gurman, the device is "roughly the thickness of an iPhone," with bezels of about a quarter-inch in black, similar to older iPad models. The body has rounded corners, with "no sharp edges whatsoever."

Below are other design details mentioned in the report:

  • The body uses Apple's "standard grey aluminium finish," with "rubber material added to the bottom to prevent the device from sliding on a desk."
  • It is powered via a USB-C port and has no built-in battery, so it must remain connected to a power source at all times.
  • The base is a "circular metal design with speaker openings arranged in multiple rings."
  • The display connects to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt the display forward or backward to adjust the angle.
  • The body does not feature any volume buttons or power buttons.
  • The front is equipped with a single FaceTime camera, with no rear camera.

Bloomberg also revealed that there is another version of the home hub "designed for wall mounting." This version is also powered by USB-C, with a base that is a "slim, square design with built-in speakers and microphones," reportedly "mounted flush against the wall below a display."

To read the full report, visit Bloomberg. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Planning to get one (or even several)? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
